package_info.why_malicious: The flatmap-stream package was intentionally modified to include crypto-stealing malicious code. It was then added as a dependency to the popular event-stream package, resulting in widespread propagation to downstream projects and even VS Code extensions. The malicious code was designed to exfiltrate sensitive data from affected systems, making the entire package chain a vector for software supply chain attacks.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the package is used in a Node.js process)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks if it is running within a targeted application (e.g., copay-dash), reads sensitive wallet data from the filesystem, and exfiltrates this data via HTTP POST to a hardcoded malicious domain, resulting in credential and asset theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code conditionally executes only in a specific application context, accesses sensitive files, and sends their contents to an external server. This is a classic pattern of targeted data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages should not access or exfiltrate user data, especially not in a targeted, stealthy manner. Legitimate packages do not contain hidden payloads that activate only in certain environments.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate telemetry or crash reporting might send non-sensitive data to a vendor, but never private keys or wallet files.
key_indicators: Obfuscated or hidden code in a dependency

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is added to flatmap-stream and published to npm.
attack_chain.leads_to: Inclusion as a dependency in event-stream package.

attack_chain.action: event-stream package (v3.3.6) is updated to depend on malicious flatmap-stream.
attack_chain.leads_to: Propagation to all projects and packages using event-stream@3.x.x.

attack_chain.action: Downstream npm packages and VS Code extensions include event-stream@3.x.x as a dependency.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in VS Code extensions.

attack_chain.action: VS Code extensions are auto-updated on developer machines, pulling in the malicious dependency.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes on developer systems at next VS Code startup.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes in the context of the developer's environment, exfiltrating sensitive data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromise of developer credentials and assets.

behavioral_signatures: Conditional execution based on environment variables or package name
Access to sensitive files (e.g., wallet.dat, private keys) in Node.js packages
Network requests to hardcoded or suspicious domains from package dependencies
Obfuscated or minified code in dependencies with low download counts
file_indicators: VS Code extensions with event-stream or flatmap-stream in their dependency tree
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to unknown or suspicious domains from developer machines
Domains associated with known malware campaigns (e.g., malicious-domain.com)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Node.js packages or VS Code extensions that include flatmap-stream or event-stream@3.x.x as dependencies. Scan for code that conditionally executes based on environment variables or package names and attempts to access and exfiltrate sensitive files. Flag any network activity from development environments to suspicious or hardcoded external domains, especially during extension or package installation and runtime. Use static analysis to detect obfuscated or hidden payloads in dependencies.
